title: Red Sailboat Lesson
subject: A small red sailboat with a white sail on a calm turquoise sea at sunset, with the low sun, its golden path on the water, and a purple mountain on the far shore.

steps.name: Blend the sunset sky
steps.summary: Blend the sunset sky from violet at the top through pink to orange.

paints.name: Twilight violet
paints.recipe: 1 part ultramarine, 1 part white, a touch of red

paints.name: Sunset pink
paints.recipe: 3 parts white, 2 parts red, 1 part ultramarine

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

paints.name: Glow gold
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 2 parts red, 2 parts white

brushes.use: covering and blending the whole sky

do: The light comes from the setting sun, low and a little left of center; every highlight faces left.
With the 1 inch flat and creamy Twilight violet, long side-to-side strokes across the top 10%.
Sunset pink to 22% down, Sunset orange to 45%, then orange with a little pink down to a straight edge at 62% (6.8 in). X-stroke each join while wet.
X-stroke Glow gold in a soft patch 39% across, 40% down. Done: a smooth gradient, white below 62%.
watch_out: Run the orange below the horizon line (54%) to 62% down; the mountain and water go over it.
Stop blending once the paint drags. Streaks are fine.

steps.name: Paint the sun
steps.summary: Paint the round cream sun in the glow.

paints.name: Sun cream
paints.recipe: 2 parts white, 1 part yellow, a touch of red

do: Let the sky dry.
With the #8 round and creamy Sun cream, dab a circle about 0.8 in wide, centered 39% across and 42.5% down, working from the center out.
Let it dry and add a second coat so no orange shows through. Done: a clean, bright round sun.
watch_out: Light over orange needs 2 coats; wait between them.
Trace a coin or bottle cap lightly in pencil first if a freehand circle is hard.

steps.name: Paint the mountain and the far shore
steps.summary: Paint the purple mountain and the dark shoreline along the horizon.

paints.name: Mountain purple
paints.recipe: 2 parts ultramarine, 1 part white, a touch of red, a touch of burnt sienna

paints.name: Shore navy
paints.recipe: 1 part ultramarine, a touch of yellow, a touch of white

brushes.use: the mountain's edge and fill, and the shoreline strip

do: Let the sky dry. Mark the horizon with a ruler: a light pencil line 54% down (5.9 in).

With the 1/2 inch flat and creamy Mountain purple, pull the mountain's top edge: from the left edge 40% down, over a low peak near the edge, sloping down to 40% across. Fill below with side-to-side strokes.
Lay the values in the table on the mountain while wet.
With Shore navy and the flat's edge, pull a straight strip across the whole width, from 50% down to the pencil line. Done: orange sky still shows from 54% to 62%.
watch_out: Keep the strip level; a tilted horizon makes the sea look like it's draining.

values.where: the strip along the horizon and the mountain's base

values.paint: Mountain purple with a little white
values.where: a few strokes along the sunlit right-hand slope

steps.name: Lay in the water
steps.summary: Lay in the water, turquoise at the horizon and deeper teal below.

paints.name: Turquoise water
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 2 parts white, 1 part yellow

paints.name: Deep teal
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

do: With the 1 inch flat and creamy Turquoise water, paint long level strokes from the navy strip down to about 70% down.
Paint Deep teal from the bottom edge up, and blend it into the turquoise while wet with long horizontal strokes.
Done: water covers everything below the strip, no white canvas anywhere.
watch_out: It may look flat and plain right now. That's the ugly stage, and it's normal.

steps.name: Add ripples to the water
steps.summary: Add short dark and light ripple dashes across the water.

paints.name: Turquoise water
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 2 parts white, 1 part yellow

paints.name: Deep teal
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

do: Let the water dry.
With the 1/2 inch flat and nearly dry Deep teal, make short horizontal dashes across the water: small and close near the horizon, longer (up to 1.5 in) toward the bottom.
Then add Turquoise water dashes with a little white between them. Done: the base still shows between the dashes.
watch_out: Don't cover the base completely; ripples are broken marks.
Try a few dashes on scrap paper first.

steps.name: Paint the sun's path on the water
steps.summary: Paint the glowing orange path of the sun on the water.

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

paints.name: Glow gold
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 2 parts red, 2 parts white

do: Let the ripples dry.

With the 1/2 inch flat and creamy Sunset orange, make short horizontal dashes in a column under the sun, shaped as in the diagram: 34% to 47% across at the horizon, widest (15% to 55%) at 70-80% down, narrowing below.
Add Glow gold dashes over the middle of the column, and a few stray orange dashes out on the left water. Done: teal shows between the dashes.
watch_out: Leave gaps between the dashes; a solid stripe looks like a road, not light on water.

steps.name: Paint the red hull
steps.summary: Paint the red hull of the boat on the water.

paints.name: Boat red
paints.recipe: 1 part red, a touch of ultramarine

do: Let the water dry.
Build the hull as in the diagram: about 2.9 in long, from 63% to 84% across. Its pointed left end rises to 57% down; the top edge slopes to about 60% at the blunt right end.
Outline it with the #6 round and creamy Boat red, then fill it in.
Let it dry and add a second coat. Done: a solid red hull on the water.
watch_out: Keep the waterline along the bottom level with the horizon; only the top edge slopes.

steps.name: Paint the sails and the mast
steps.summary: Paint the two white sails, the mast, and the boom.

paints.name: Sail white
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow

paints.name: Sail shadow
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 1 part ultramarine, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow

paints.name: Mast brown
paints.recipe: 3 parts burnt sienna, 2 parts ultramarine, 1 part red, 1 part white

do: Let the hull dry.
Build the sails as in the diagram: the mast's line rises from the hull at 72% across to 26% down (about 3.4 in tall).
With the #6 round and creamy Sail white, fill the left triangle (lower corner 64% across) and the right one (down to 57% down, out to 81% across). Two coats.
While wet, lay the values in the table.
Let it dry. With the liner and inky Mast brown, pull the mast, then the boom along the right sail's bottom edge.
watch_out: Rest your wrist on a dry part of the canvas for a straight mast.
Try a liner line on scrap paper first.

values.where: down the right side of each sail, away from the sun
the rest of the sails, brightest on the left, facing the sun

steps.name: Paint the boat's reflection
steps.summary: Paint the boat's red and white reflection in the water.

paints.name: Boat red
paints.recipe: 1 part red, a touch of ultramarine

paints.name: Sail white
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow

paints.name: Mast brown
paints.recipe: 3 parts burnt sienna, 2 parts ultramarine, 1 part red, 1 part white

do: Let the water dry.
With the 1/2 inch flat and creamy Boat red, make short horizontal dashes just under the hull, from 63% to 67% down, as wide as the hull.
With Sail white, make broken horizontal dashes from 68% down to about 94% down, getting narrower toward the bottom.
With the liner and inky Mast brown, pull a wavy line down the middle at 72% across. Done: teal shows between the dashes.
watch_out: Keep it broken: a solid reflection looks like a second boat.

steps.name: Add the brightest highlights
steps.summary: Add the brightest sparkles on the water and the trim on the hull.

paints.name: Sun cream
paints.recipe: 2 parts white, 1 part yellow, a touch of red

paints.name: Sail white
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow

do: Let everything dry.
With the #4 round and creamy Sun cream, add short dashes in the middle of the sun path, most near the horizon.
With the liner and Sail white, pull a thin line along the hull's top edge. Done: the finished painting.
watch_out: Fewer highlights look brighter; stop before you think you're done.
